Mature, grounded color; rich but restrained contrast. Luminous, dramatic lighting. Gritty, raw texture; avoid polished digital smoothness. Cinematic, immersive viewpoint; heroic but grounded.
World: Alice, a young Victorian English girl, among talking animals, card courtiers and odd Wonderland folk. A Victorian child's dress and pinafore for Alice; period robes, waistcoats and hats for others.
Character: Alice: a young Victorian English girl of about seven or eight, slender and small-boned with a child's build, fair skin, long loose hair that falls into her bright eager eyes and is tossed back from her face, and a round, earnest face. She wears a Victorian child's dress with a pinafore over it, with stockings and buttoned shoes on her feet, and carries nothing else of note.
Layout: the same figure shown three times side by side, evenly spaced, on one plain, even mid-grey background: (1) full-length standing view facing the viewer; (2) full-length standing view in a three-quarter turn; (3) a large head-and-shoulders close-up portrait in three-quarter view that shows the face clearly. Calm, neutral standing pose and expression, arms relaxed. Face, hair, build, garments and colours identical in all three views. No other people or figures.
Absolutely no text of any kind anywhere: no names, labels, captions, titles, letters, numbers, arrows, colour swatches, rulers, frames, borders or panel dividers.
No likeness of any real actor, performer or public figure.

Never present the scene as a painting on a wall, gallery piece, framed artwork, fresco, mural, poster, manuscript page, or printed illustration. Do not show canvas texture, paper edges, matting, border, mockup, or surrounding room. The depicted world must fill the image edge-to-edge.
